content.title: Mexico and Brazil Legends Draw in Star-Studded Exhibition Match
content.text: Published Apr 20, 2026 - 07:33 Last Update Apr 20, 2026 - 07:33 Smallest Font Largest Font Mexican football legends played to a 2-2 draw against Brazil's iconic stars during an exhibition match held Sunday, April 19, 2026, at the Estadio Banorte. The high-profile encounter featured world-renowned figures including Ronaldinho, Kaka, Rafael Marquez, and Cuauhtemoc Blanco in front of thousands of fans. SoccerOribe Peralta led the Mexican attack with two goals, securing the equalizer after Brazil took early leads through Adriano and Kaka. The match served as a nostalgic celebration for fans in Mexico City, appearing on the calendar less than two months before the start of the 2026 World Cup. The Brazilian side, coached by 1970 World Cup winner Jairzinho, opened the scoring when Adriano converted a chip shot following a pass from Ronaldinho. Mexico responded quickly through Luis "El Matador" Hernandez, who found the net after receiving a ball from Jared Borgetti according to as.com. LiveSporting Events Brazil regained the advantage when Kaka maneuvered past the Mexican defense and dinked the ball over goalkeeper Oswaldo Sanchez. However, Mexico leveled the score again before halftime when Peralta connected with a cross from Andres Guardado to beat Julio Cesar. Miguel "Piojo" Herrera returned to the technical area to manage the Mexican squad, which utilized a rotating lineup including Miguel Layun, Pavel Pardo, and Gerardo Torrado. The second half saw several emotional moments, including standing ovations for Rafael Marquez and Ronaldinho as they were substituted as reported by Mediotiempo.Security for the event involved more than 4,000 police officers coordinated by the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection to manage the large crowds and traffic closures surrounding the stadium. Despite several close chances for both teams in the closing minutes, the match ended in a stalemate. "The Kaiser" Rafael Marquez made way for Ricardo Osorio during the final portion of the game, while the Brazilian bench featured depth with players like Djalminha and Juninho Paulista.
